terminal_name: Puerto de la Luz LNG Terminal
topic: Project cancellation (2025): unfavourable environmental ruling and sponsor withdrawal
wiki_text: On October 15, 2025, the Directorate General for Ecological Transition and Climate Action of the Canary Islands Government issued an unfavourable Environmental Impact Declaration (DIA desfavorable) for Totisa Energia's proposed LNG storage, regasification and power-generation plant at the Puerto de la Luz (Las Palmas de Gran Canaria), ending roughly six years of permitting. Following the negative ruling, Totisa Energia S.L.U. withdrew its application for the port concession; the Las Palmas Port Authority's board of directors accepted the withdrawal and ordered the return of the company's provisional guarantee. The decision followed sustained local opposition: in November 2024 both the Las Palmas city council and the Cabildo (island council) had formally rejected the project over sustainability, safety and health concerns and urged the regional government to do the same. The Port Authority indicated it would pursue alternative arrangements (e.g. storage tanks) to secure LNG bunkering supply for ships. With this outcome the project is effectively cancelled.

topic: Rebrand to Musel E-Hub / Musel Energy Hub and multimodal/bioLNG services
wiki_text: After Enagas and Reganosa completed their transaction in September 2023 (Enagas 75%, Reganosa 25%) to create an energy hub in the northwest of the Iberian Peninsula, the El Musel terminal in the Port of Gijon was rebranded as 'Musel E-Hub' (also styled 'Musel Energy Hub'). The terminal began commercial operations in August 2023 (first commercial vessel, the Gaslog Warsaw, on August 11, 2023) after long being held in reserve following its 2012 mechanical completion. It comprises two 150,000 m3 storage tanks and an 800,000 Nm3/h send-out capacity (~8 bcm/y) and operates as a multimodal logistics hub (ship and truck reloading, transshipment). A Spanish official-gazette resolution (BOE-A-2024-15568, July 26, 2024) raised the plant's maximum annual regasification capacity to 11,744 GWh/year (from 10,969 GWh/year), allowing continuous-regime operation. In November 2025 the hub began supplying bio-LNG to ships and tankers.
